It already puts the red-flowered Ian Morris photograph under G. longicuspis and the two cream-flowered photographs under G. mimosoides. Their composition matches the two named PICK files. descriptionReviewNotes.reason: Both the source manuscript and book Y page 229 print cm for the width. This appears to be a unit typo: the account describes narrow sickle-shaped leaves, the photographs agree, and Flora of Australia 17A (2000), p. 375 describes G. mimosoides leaves 6.5-40 cm long and 6-50 mm wide. The narrower local range has not been independently verified. Record for researcher review; do not silently rewrite the manuscript or existing admin entry.

speciesLevelPhotoPolicy.decision: The owner authorizes candidate species-level photographs on the nine listed subspecies/variety accounts. Public photo captions retain the species binomial, while account headings and descriptions retain the full taxon. This is permission to illustrate, not confirmation of the subspecies/variety shown. Each selected file remains an explicit hash-pinned allocation.
speciesLevelPhotoPolicy.ownerContext: The owner suggests these subspecies/varieties often represent the locally familiar expression of the species, specifically citing Alstonia spectabilis subsp. ophioxyloides. Recorded as editorial context; not treated as independent taxonomic verification.
